title: Next.js SWR Three-Layer Cache — Stale Live Data
relevance: Directly covers SWR caching/deduplication patterns and Next.js force-dynamic / Cache-Control patterns. All three layers (route cache, HTTP response cache, browser fetch cache) must be fixed simultaneously for live data routes. Also documents known regressions: balance, portfolio, and BalanceChip fetcher are still missing cache layers.
summary: Next.js 16.2.1 has three independent caching layers that all silently serve stale data. Every live-data API route needs (1) `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, (2) `Cache-Control: no-store` in the NextResponse headers, and (3) `fetch(url, { cache: 'no-store' })` in every SWR fetcher. Fixing any one or two layers is insufficient — the symptom is identical stale data with no error at every partial-fix stage. SWR's `refreshInterval` fires correctly but returns cached data; the bug is invisible in DevTools Network tab. A shared fetcher module (`market-fetcher.ts`) is the canonical home for the Layer 3 fix. Known remaining regressions as of 2026-04-13: `balance/route.ts`, `portfolio/route.ts`, `markets/route.ts` (Layers 1+2 missing), `BalanceChip.tsx` fetcher (Layer 3 missing).

title: Turbopack Instrumentation Worker unref() Kills setInterval Before Recurring Polls Fire
relevance: Covers React/Node.js timer cleanup via references (useRef/setInterval handle management). The anti-pattern of calling unref() on a timer that is the sole handle keeping a context alive is directly applicable to any deferred/cleanup pattern using setTimeout or setInterval references.
summary: In Next.js 16.2.1 + Turbopack dev mode, `register()` in `instrumentation.ts` runs in an isolated worker with no other event-loop handles. Calling `setInterval(...).unref()` there causes the worker's event loop to drain immediately after the first async poll resolves — the interval never fires again. Fix: remove `unref()`. The interval's referenced state is what keeps the worker alive. Rule: `unref()` is safe in a process with other persistent handles (HTTP listener, file watchers); it is lethal when the timer is the sole handle. The inverse problem in production: forgetting `unref()` prevents graceful shutdown — use explicit `clearInterval()` in a SIGTERM handler instead.

title: Client-Side LMSR Payout Calculator in BetSheet
relevance: Covers deferred input sync patterns (slider onChange → synchronous client-side computation replacing a 400ms debounced server round-trip), balance/financial input validation (staleness guard on submit), and CoinSlider as a custom input component. The staleness guard pattern is a template for any financial input that commits based on a price seen earlier.
summary: Replaced a debounced server-action preview (`previewTrade`, 400ms lag) with synchronous client-side LMSR math from `src/lib/lmsr.ts` (pure arithmetic, no I/O). Key patterns: (1) CoinSlider uses `<input type='range'>` with 44px touch target and `onChange={e => parseInt(e.target.value, 10)}`. (2) Payout preview runs on every slider tick — no debounce needed for pure math. (3) Staleness guard on submit: fire a fresh `fetch(url, { cache: 'no-store' })` before the server action; compare `|freshPrice[outcome] - cachedPrice[outcome]| > 0.02`; block and show updated payout if stale. Always check the *selected outcome's* price (not hardcoded priceYes). (4) `buyShares` returns no `priceAfter` — compute post-trade prices client-side using `result.shares + local quantities`. (5) `quantityYes`/`quantityNo` arrive as decimal strings from Drizzle — always `parseFloat()` before passing to LMSR. (6) Three-layer cache is load-bearing for staleness correctness: if any layer is missing, the fresh-fetch on submit may return a cached response. Rule: client-side for previews, server action for the actual transaction.

title: Next.js Financial App: Code Review Patterns & Fixes
relevance: Covers balance and financial input validation patterns: race conditions in financial transactions, idempotency keys on coin ledger entries, UTC normalization for date comparisons, and the overall checklist for financial server actions. Also relevant to any balance-related route work (balance/route.ts is called out as missing cache layers in the SWR doc).
summary: Comprehensive patterns for financial actions in this codebase. Key items: (1) No pre-check SELECT before INSERT — catch Postgres error code `23505` instead (NULL != NULL bypasses naive checks). (2) Double-claim guards require `SELECT FOR UPDATE` inside a transaction — timestamp checks outside a lock have a race window. (3) Every coin ledger entry needs a `referenceId` as an idempotency key. (4) Concurrent trades use optimistic locking with a `version` column + 3-attempt retry loop. (5) UTC normalization: use `Date.UTC(...)` not `setHours(0,0,0,0)` — the latter uses server local timezone, wrong in serverless. (6) Payout distribution: use VALUES CTE batch updates, not O(N) individual DB round-trips. (7) Admin auth must be centralized in `isAdmin()` — env var absence must default to deny. Prevention checklist: no pre-check SELECT, `SELECT FOR UPDATE` for claim guards, optimistic locking for concurrent mutations, `referenceId` on every ledger entry, `Date.UTC` for all timestamp comparisons.

title: Mobile FeedCard: Expandable Bet Tray & Nav Bar Clearance Fixes
relevance: Covers pointer-event and interaction state patterns in touch/mobile UI. Documents the established FeedCard rule: interaction state (isPaused, isBetExpanded) uses conditional render mount/unmount, not CSS toggling. Also documents the deactivate()/doStop promise-guard pattern that governs where any state reset must live — relevant to any component with async play/pause or drag-to-dismiss interactions.
summary: Two systems coexist in FeedCard and must never be mixed: (1) Density system (full/compact/minimal) — controlled externally, uses `DENSITY_BUTTON_STYLE` opacity + pointer-events CSS. (2) Local interaction state (isPaused, isBetExpanded) — uses `{state && (...)}` conditional render (mount/unmount). Any new boolean state controlling visible UI must be reset in `doStop()` inside `deactivate()` (not outside the closure), in `setDensity('minimal')`, and on every user action that closes the feature. The `deactivate()` method guards a play/pause promise race — resets placed outside `doStop()` are overwritten when the async promise resolves. Card body `onClick` must check interaction state first and return early before delegating to `onTap()`. Use `e.stopPropagation()` on buttons inside overlays. For mobile nav clearance in h-screen containers: use `style={{ bottom: 'calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px) + 5rem)' }}` — Tailwind cannot compose env() variables without a custom plugin.
